# Rig checklist

In-game checks waiting for a batched rig run. A rig run never gates a merge. Each slice lists its checks in its PR description. After merge the coordinator copies them here, and removes a check once a rig run passes it at a build that still contains the change. This list authorizes no run.

Every check runs in a named disposable FT city in the isolated rig profile, never in Peter's ordinary save. Autosave is off before every measured window, including after a reload, and is restored at cleanup.

Detailed specs: [F8 §7](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/blob/a3a6c8db8686f4382ac3cf941010e0b614e48805/docs/plans/f8-capability-boundaries.md#7-in-game-checks-for-the-batched-rig), [F9 §7](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/blob/a3a6c8db8686f4382ac3cf941010e0b614e48805/docs/plans/f9-city-acceptance.md#7-in-game-checks-for-the-next-batched-rig), [E6 §7](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/blob/a3a6c8db8686f4382ac3cf941010e0b614e48805/docs/plans/e6-carts-food-trucks.md#7-in-game-checks-for-the-batched-rig), [F4 plan](plans/f4-perf-gate.md), [11j report](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/blob/a3a6c8db8686f4382ac3cf941010e0b614e48805/docs/checks/rig-2026-11-11j-mac-results.md), [12b report](checks/rig-2026-11-12b-mac-results.md). Checks written before 10 November are in the [docs history tag](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/tree/docs-history-2026-11-10/docs/checks); many test save migration, which no longer exists.

## GR-5 gates (from 19 November 2026)

The gates are in the [register](decisions/2026-11-10-city-direction.md#gr-5-acceptance-gates-19-november-2026). The mod-versus-no-mod heap footprint (D), the RSS allowance (E) and census growth after a single retime (F) are reported only. The memory verdict is the leak rule. Earlier results below were judged under the gates in force at the time.

Every GR-5 rig run from now on must:

1. Run the repeated-cycle leak measurement: at least three 1->2->1 retimes in one fresh process, each waited to completion. After each, read the retained census (total and per type), managed heap (live after forced GC and the gap to the no-mod reference), process RSS and the mod's native counters (owned, live and unmerged meshes, live vertices, bake scratch). Read the retained census at the same matched point each time.
2. Record autosave suppression per check: the original value, and the value verified off after each reload and before and after each window.

### RLO 1.0.6 checks 2 and 3

Original `rlo_option` read: stored=null, live=true, original_saved=false. Off-before-load used `op rlo_option {"action":"set","name":"living_population","value":false}`, verified stored=0/live=false, then a cold restart and load of `FT RLO 13d Owned 12`. The eligible owned shop is `FT RLO 13d Food v1`, `ba:street_fourthavenue#19`, with ready=true, staffed register, croissants $5 and normal free paper bags. The player remained outside. Native shop logging was installed only after all performance windows.

| Sales observation | PC new paid receipts / cents | Native visits / paid croissants / free bags | Revenue | Dropped / hook faults |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Off, 12:00–14:00 | 3 / 1,500 | 3 / 3 / 3 | $110→$125 | 0 / 0 |
| First toggle attempt, 12:00–14:00 | 7 / 3,500 | 7 / 7 / 7 | $110→$145 | 0 / 0 |

Saved receipt keys were compared with pre-interval live keys; every new receipt is paid, 500 cents, croissant, with no extra paid line. The native log has no additional visits/products beyond the matched receipts and free bags. Both intervals suppressed two native draws and two hourly batches. Hooks list all five `CustomerEntriesCalculatorFactory.* [non-Harmony]` RLO replacements as overruled; checkout stayed active in the off interval and first toggle attempt. Extracted saves have schema 1.

Check 3 first cold-loaded the owned checkpoint with Living on. At speed 1 it set off, waited five real seconds, set on, waited five seconds, then read capability status. Exactly one Player.log transition line per change appeared within **0.443 / 0.236 seconds** from each setter call. Status was `Living population on, 2 toggle(s) this session`. The seven sales are positive matching evidence for the interval, but their timing does not establish selling after the transitions. A separate 14:00–17:30 observation added no receipts, revenue or PC purchases (7→7).

To obtain that missing observation, a fresh process loaded the earlier `FT RLO 13d Food v1` at 08:00, advanced at speed 20 to 10:30, confirmed an active coordinator with one committed image, then resumed at speed 1 for the same off/five-seconds/on/five-seconds sequence. The runtime stopped during this repeat, before it could report either transition; by 12:30 FoodDiagnostics.active=false, capability status `start refused (clock.city)`, checkout not checked, purchases=0. Exact error:

```text
System.ArgumentException: Cannot retime a maximum-size native car route without splitting its current edge.
Parameter name: state
```

The retained stack names `PersistentCity.Core.TravelTiming.Apply` then `PopulationRuntime.UpdateCity`; raw log `<stage>/rlo-toggle-early-Player.log`, first stop line 2722. The repeat's resume operation was `call time {"speed":1,"pause":false,"keep_needs":true}`, after the speed-20 preparation. No causal claim about the RLO setter is made. The failed fixture's later checkpoint retains the documented refusal marker and is not a recovery fixture. No production fix or further investigation was attempted.

Restore succeeded through `op rlo_option {"action":"restore","name":"living_population"}`; independent readback returned **stored=null, live=true, original_saved=false**, matching the original. No RLO file was edited.

### Living transitions and paid receipts

Original op read: stored=null, live=true, original_saved=false. For each transition the run resumed at speed 1, called `rlo_option set` with name=living_population and the required boolean, waited five real seconds, and read capability/FoodDiagnostics. Off sales interval was 10:30–12:30; on interval was 12:30–14:30. No sale probe fabricated a receipt. Native shop_log was enabled only for this check, after all rush-hour observations, and stopped afterward. The owned fixture shop is `ba:street_fourthavenue#19`.

| Interval | Paid receipts newly arriving in interval | Paid cents |
|---|---|---|
| Living off | 0 | 0 |
| Living on after second transition | 0 | 0 |

The on count compares saved keys after the on interval against all off-interval keys. Before the toggle, FoodDiagnostics already showed zero purchases and the live key set contained no paid food receipts. The ready shop held 100 croissants at $5, a staffed register and free paper bags, with revenue $0. No causal claim about the option toggle is made: the required continuing-sale evidence did not occur in the two observed intervals. Both native shop_log snapshots report purchases=0, dropped=0 and hook_faults=0. Revenue stayed $0 and croissant stock stayed 100. Final food-contract readback reports capabilitiesPassed=true, firstFailure=null, coordinator mode=Active, images=1, Commits=1 and Refusals=0. These reads establish an active contract, without explaining why no sales arrived. Raw extracted PC keys and native shop visit replies are retained separately. Exact transition lines:

```text
[Mod:PersistentCity] RLO Living population on -> Living population off during play; Persistent City keeps owning its shops, crowds and traffic.
[Mod:PersistentCity] RLO Living population off -> Living population on during play; Persistent City keeps owning its shops, crowds and traffic.
```

Restore op and independent read both returned stored=null, live=true, original_saved=false. No RLO file was edited.

Every exported mod-work spike is listed (126 rows: day 16, night 2, street 108). The compact JSON keeps three largest spike examples per window; complete frame/component lists are in this table and the hash-indexed raw end replies. The dominant self component attributes the measured mod work; it does not establish an allocating method or GC cause. `pc gc stop` exposes aggregate GC pause counts/percentiles but no per-pause Unity frame IDs; those pauses cannot be assigned exact frames from its response. Spikes are reported, not chased. Whole-frame spikes remain separate from mod-work; complete raw whole-frame records are in the stage.

### Visual check and exact failures

Separate cold background graphics rig-test start, same fixture Tuesday 15:30, player x=215,z=0. Nine 1600×900 PNGs inspected: first close view includes a dressed walker in a red jacket and dark trousers; its return contains dressed walkers but the target is distant. The second close/return view is occluded by a building. Five pan stills contain sparse dressed walkers or empty/occluded sidewalk. No undressed body is seen in the inspected images; the images do not prove no invisible body or brief appearance flash, or unchanged visuals versus a synchronized baseline.

Two native walker handles were selected. After an 8 s camera-away interval, the first handle (`walker-a003dd287c154421abf30362d533be80`) still answered screen_pos and camera-follow; its return capture occurred after 11.914 s. Expected: dressed bodies, same look per resident before and after, and none of "Appearance meshes unavailable", "Empty appearance" or "Merged body ..." in the log.

Five native walker handles were followed, moved out of view for 8 s, and queried on return. Three handles remained readable and two returned ops_view_stale_target for both screen_pos get and camera follow. Return delays were approximately 12–14 s. All five old handles returned ops_view_stale_target after the bounded reload, which completed in 175.1 s without an ops_load_* failure or cold restart. Eleven 1600×900 captures were inspected. ### Look observations and exact failures

Five fresh native walker handles were selected one per cycle. Player and camera moved from x=215,z=0 to a verified native-walker ground point x=317.531,z=-122.201805 (159.5 m away; configured body radius 120 m), waited 8 s, returned, and waited 5 s. Three old handles (0, 1, 3) returned ops_view_stale_target for both screen_pos get and camera follow; two (2, 4) remained readable. Return steps took 17.0–17.5 s. The bounded reload completed in 86.3 s, with no ops_load_* failure or cold restart; all five old handles then returned ops_view_stale_target. Fourteen 1600x900 captures were inspected. Pair 2 shows an orange-haired figure in dark clothes and pink shoes before and after; pair 4 shows a red-haired figure in a green top and tan lower clothing before and after. Release of those two bodies is not established. Other pairs lose the selected subject or show unrelated dressed figures after return. The purple-shirted player avatar is not counted as a resident. No undressed body was observed. Curbside cars are visible, but saved-curb identities/assignments are not exported; several cars appear raised above the pavement in the stills, without proof of a new regression. The after-reload wide shot shows curbside cars and the player; the old residents cannot be found by identity. The required five-resident same-look proof and saved-curb proof are NOT RUN / tooling gaps, not replaced by these observations. Sparse stills cannot rule out invisible bodies or flashes. Both full process logs have zero occurrences of Appearance meshes unavailable, Empty appearance and Merged body. The first look controller stopped on a refused x=600,z=0 teleport; a second x=0,z=0 probe was also refused. Both exact errors are below; the same graphics process continued from verified ground.

### Literal Expected lines and outcomes

**PR #284**

## In-game checks
All locked-PC, none input-only. Fixture FT GR5 13f Timing v1, 1,000 residents / 2,000 visitors.
1. **Day GC window.** Setup: clock 15:30, idle camera, speed 1 after a 20→1 change. Steps: 600 s gc window. Expected: report gen0, pause p95, heap, mod, physical, advance and every segment and sub-segment against rig 15f. `mod_routes_rebuild` well below 83.9 MB; food, planning and citizen leaves below 15f.
2. **Night GC window.** Same at 01:00. Expected: the same report; `mod_routes_rebuild` well below 58.7 MB.
3. **Street window.** Setup: daytime. Steps: 600 s street window with pans and a 1→2→1 rate change. Expected: UpdateCity and mod-work p95 under 5 ms; every ≥30 ms spike listed with phase, detail, sub and gc_phase, none from retime/`mod_routes_rebuild`, `physical_spawn_appearance` or `mod_rlo`; `phase_spikes_30ms`, retained and `phase_spikes_truncated=false`; whole-frame p95/max reported separately; the `Clock retime: body release … ms over N updates` lines copied.
4. **Look stability.** Setup: daytime street. Steps: follow 5 residents through a speed change (body release and reacquire), then reload and find them again. Expected: dressed, animated bodies with the same look before and after, and none of "Appearance meshes unavailable", "Empty appearance" or "Merged body" in Player.log.
5. **Release frames.** Setup: daytime street with bodies and cars on screen. Steps: change speed 1→2 and watch the release updates. Expected: bodies and cars not yet released hold still or fade for at most a few frames with no visible jump, and no body stays behind after the new population appears. Report `RetimeReleaseSteps` (the N in the log line), how many of those updates the ambient walker restore took, and the mod-work time of each release update, including the car-pool and body-pool updates. No walker that RLO took over for an incident or ragdoll during the release gets its collider re-enabled or starts walking.


**PR #282**

## In-game checks
All locked-PC, none input-only.
1. **Day GC window.** Setup: FT GR5 13f Timing v1, 1,000 residents / 2,000 visitors, clock 15:30, idle camera, speed 1 after a 20 to 1 change. Steps: run a 600 s gc window. Expected: report gen0, pause p95, heap, mod, physical, advance and every segment and sub-segment vs 15d. physical_spawn_appearance well below 33.5 MB. The look diagnostics show `fast merges` > 0 and `failed merges` 0. mod_routes_nodes near 0.5 MB if the rate returned to one seen earlier in the session.
2. **Night GC window.** Same at 01:00. Expected: appearance well below 14.1 MB; report every segment vs 15d night.
3. **Street window.** Setup: same fixture, daytime. Steps: 600 s street window with pans and at least one clock-rate change and back. Expected: report UpdateCity and mod-work p95 and every ≥30 ms spike with phase, detail, sub and gc_phase, plus whole-frame p95/max separately. The phase recorder reports `phase_spikes_30ms`, `phase_spikes_retained` and `phase_spikes_truncated=false`. Note any spike from retime/mod_routes_rebuild, physical_spawn_appearance or mod_rlo with its whole-frame time.
4. **Look stability.** Setup: same fixture, daytime street. Steps: follow 5 residents through body release and reacquire, change speed once, reload and find them again. Expected: dressed and animated bodies with blendshapes applied, the same look per resident before and after, `failed merges` 0, and none of "Appearance meshes unavailable", "Empty appearance" or "Merged body" in Player.log.

**PR #246**

4. **Unrentable home footprint (input-only).** Setup: the city from check 1. Steps: pick three residential buildings with no rentable interior, including one rotated off the world axes and one with a yard or sidewalk under it. Compare each Home place's area evidence (footprint x floors x 0.6) and floor count with the visible building. Expected: footprint within about 1.5x of the visible ground area and floors within one of the visible storeys. `ReadFootprint` takes the world-axis bounds of every enabled non-trigger collider, so rotated buildings and ground colliders read large. If this check fails, the read moves to the main mesh in local space.
5. **Unreadable and empty tally (input-only).** Steps: read the `unrentable homes ... unreadable=N empty=M` line after load. Expected: buildings under one storey count as empty, not unreadable, and the omitted-places warning only counts unreadable ones.

### B — #293 check 2 and #290 checks 2–4: reload / quit consistency

**PASS** for cold reload, immediate reload and save-then-quit. The first immediate load/stop dispatches followed trigger returns in 2.197 / 1.535 s, with `in_progress=true` and `compress_thread_alive=true`. Two repeat cases add a diagnostic read before dispatch: both observed `mode=background`, then confirmed compression still alive before load/stop. A newly loaded runtime resets its last-save mode field, so its initial `main-thread` value is not used to describe the preceding save.

Check-1 native serialized input and final file have identical `foodtrucks:state`: **2491 characters**, SHA-256 `df5001bd08bd28c5be3795d8363426b4e21dc4596241575279b8a032b8c66b45`; trucks **0→0**. This fixture has no populated trucks. The source fixture text is 2,474 characters; Street Food rewrites its own version/save counter before serialization. ### C — #293 check 3 / #290 check 5: forced refusal

**PASS.** Fault-points build staged while stopped/owned. Launcher uses inherited `subprocess.Popen` environment; `PC_FAULT_POINT=save:writer-refusal` was set only for the fault start and unset immediately afterwards in the controller. Saved only to the new `FT RIGTMP-fault-refusal-17k-mac` slot, never the fixture. Actual diagnostics:

```json
{
  "mode": "background",
  "writer.success": false,
  "writer.error": "Population save refused: Forced background save refusal (PC_FAULT_POINT=save:writer-refusal).",
  "compress.splice": "Spliced",
  "failed_marker": "failed:2",
  "previous_payload_preserved": true,
  "foodtrucks_input_output_equal": true,
  "foodtrucks_chars": 2490,
  "foodtrucks_sha256": "0132030fad7e719dd0dbeef4dd6a8af70a4a7d90a839aae6a4b66e1a94a6e788",
  "pending_token": false,
  "cleanup_mode": "background",
  "cleanup_splice": "Spliced"
}
```

The previous PC payload remained 6,050,970 characters. The failed marker is literally `failed:2`; the splice result is literally `Spliced` (not a fabricated combined “Spliced failed” field). Reload left `attached=false` and logged the refusal below. The new runtime’s refused counter is 0 because no city attached; that is not a successful activation. `pc population status` returned the exact unknown-command usage under tooling gaps; the refusal verdict uses the failed marker and startup log.

```text
[Mod:PersistentCity] Persistent City stopped: Load a synchronized pre-failure checkpoint or another city to restart Persistent City. This stopped save stays refused; native time continues. Save epoch refused: Population save refused: Forced background save refusal (PC_FAULT_POINT=save:writer-refusal). Native calendar continues; Persistent City is stopped. Unprocessed Persistent City demand is lost, not replayed. The original population payload is retained. Native saves remain playable with Persistent City stopped.
```

Cleanup: game stopped, standard package restaged, no fault variable in the standard launch, fault slot deleted with `after.exists=false`, and one ordinary save confirmed `background` / `Spliced` before D.

Observer mode: `background`; after stopping street, reported free memory **76%**. The run retained 16g’s observer budget of at least 75% reported free memory for the roughly 9 GB graphics footprint. No OS setting changed. Capture/visual review results follow; a rendered image alone does not prove five-resident look equality or animation.

Travelling residents were selected by #96/#97 resident identity, not native walker handle. Follow requests were issued before 1→2→1; pc:282 was already absent by its before get/follow. Gets after the final speed change ran at 1×, with bounded retries for absent bodies. A paused look save wrote only this run’s exclusively created `FT RIGTMP-GR5-17k-mac`, followed by reload/autosave verification; no replay from the old sealed checkpoint was needed. Before each reload get, the player and camera returned to the last observed journey position. Logical identity without a current body is not counted as re-binding. Pointer/hover remains Peter’s playtest.

Appearance error-string counts across retained log copies: `{"Appearance meshes unavailable": 0, "Empty appearance": 0, "Merged body": 0}`. Copies can overlap; zero is exact, nonzero totals would require de-duplication by process.

PARTIAL. Background rendering was admitted at 76% reported free memory. Four of five residents acquired current bodies after the rate changes (pc:403, c3, c370, c266); their generations changed. pc:282's initial walker identity existed, but its before get was already absent. After save/reload, pc:403 reacquired a current body; the other four were AtPlace/Leisure and absent during 1x retries. All five logical resident IDs remained kind=resident. The installed overlay returns donor_id=null, donor_reason=ops_view_walker_donor_unexposed despite the tested head including #295.

All fourteen subject PNGs and one post-panel-close street PNG were inspected. The ten before images are obstructed by the Campaigns panel; before-0 is mostly white, and before-1 through before-4 show only partial bodies through/around the panel. pc:403's reacquired pair is clear: blond hair, red jacket, white shirt, dark trousers, brown shoes, with a changed crouched/upright pose. ### A — release and reacquire

Cold loaded the sealed fixture, confirmed autosave suppression, replayed at 1× and waited for physical population preflight. Initial discovery ran before that preflight and found 45 unbound non-evidence walkers; fresh discovery after `Physical population active` selected five travelling residents with `binding.source: persistent_city`. ### Findings

**Collection-frame tail:** day worst collection frame 11445 is 162.212 ms with 0.929 ms UpdateCity; repeat frame 4737 is 710.617 ms with 0.376 ms UpdateCity. pause_ms_without_mod p95 is 127.552 / 676.479 ms, nearly the full sampler tails. Neither collection frame is a retained ≥30 ms union spike. The tails are predominantly outside mod work; these exports do not identify the game/native/host work responsible. Night also has a 151.784 ms collection frame with 0.317 ms UpdateCity. The one repeat mod-work spike is a different frame, gc_phase none.

Heap reads occur at different seams: the sampler context is captured before constructing its report, while final GcDiagnostics follows report/export operations. Night GcDiagnostics before window: 1,452,376,064 / 1,399,271,424 B heap/used; sampler context: 1,469,153,280 / 1,365,622,784 B; post-window projection: 1,502,707,712 / 1,478,909,952 B. An additional collection occurs outside the sampler by that last read. The evidence does not isolate which work changed the heap.

The census suppresses zero-object roots and lists up to 48 positive roots. The road +30 s read counted one RoadRoutes and had no `static.RoadRoutes.donor` row. That rules out a second retained RoadRoutes instance. It cannot tell a donor that points at the live planner from a cleared donor, so live donor ownership is inferred. `runtime.routes` reported no value at any F read, and no road objects are attributed to it. Each settings or runtime row is charged only for objects the census first reaches through that field. Cells give bytes / scanned bytes / objects.

### Findings

- The PC day reference recorded 13 gen0 collections in 600 s with Persistent City absent. Candidate steady day recorded 14 at the same start time. Both exceeded the five-collection target.

- A steady had 4.17 gen0 per 10,000 sampler frames vs 3.99 on provisional Mac 16q. The gate remains a count per 600 s. Sustained render throughput and fixture population differ.

- A repeat had 4.01 gen0 per 10,000 sampler frames vs 4.89 on provisional Mac 16q. The gate remains a count per 600 s. Sustained render throughput and fixture population differ.

- B night had 3.71 gen0 per 10,000 sampler frames vs 3.96 on provisional Mac 16q. The gate remains a count per 600 s. Sustained render throughput and fixture population differ.

### Exact operation errors and tooling gaps

- The Windows checkout’s `python scripts/agent call load {"name":"FT GR5 13f Timing v1"}` uses SSH for the bridge call and returned `ssh: Could not resolve hostname homepc: No such host is known.` The verified local bridge returned `No save named 'FT GR5 13f Timing v1'. FT saves: …` and accepted the fresh FT city. Lifecycle calls and rig file operations remained on the PC.

- The probe builder requires output below its worktree build directory and rejected the initial external output with `Output must be below this checkout ignored build directory`. The documented default build succeeded.

- Installed Ops lags #104 slot identity on Mac and #105 Mac stop handling. Neither capability is part of A–H or N. The installed player and Ops overlay remained at their start revision.

- `a-repeat/error.json`. scripts/agent status: PID identity mismatch; refusing to control this process

  ```text
  At <rig-root>\Agent-Windows.ps1:87 char:102
  + ... ed_ticks) { throw 'PID identity mismatch; refusing to control this pr ...
  +                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
      + CategoryInfo          : OperationStopped: (PID identity mi...ol this process:String) [], RuntimeException

  ```

  The status read refused control; the restoration status read later reported running=False ([restoration](#restoration-and-evidence)).

The export had no row dominated by the retime sub. Its conservative all-frame bound was 8.202 ms. Unlisted frames are bounded by the smallest of the 16 retained top-frame totals (7.299 ms, plus rounding). On listed frames, the retime sub is bounded by the dominant sub. When a different sub dominates, its time can also be subtracted from the frame’s mod total because the recorder uses a shared advancing detail timestamp. The 37.196 ms spike spent 36.398 ms in the planning sub, leaving at most 0.800 ms for the retime sub. Frame 42,802 supplies the largest bound at 8.202 ms including rounding. 16q reported 11.559 ms and PC 19c 18.634 ms using the earlier method.

### Findings

- A steady’s longest collection frame was 16017 at 208.192 ms. UpdateCity took 143.826 ms and the GC marker took 40.5226 ms. The frame recorder attributed 142.142 ms to `mod_optional_stops`, with 0 grow operations. 16q’s largest steady collection was in physical spawn grow with a much larger GC marker.
- Largest repeat and night collection frames · A retime frame 9516 · total 848.842 ms, UpdateCity 0.749 ms, GC marker 34.6125 ms / B night frame 22286 · total 102.999 ms, UpdateCity 1.660 ms, GC marker 26.4523 ms. The repeat frame had about 813.5 ms outside the measured UpdateCity and Unity GC times.
- The B modwork export grew the Mono heap by +35,504,128 B. The final read was 24,128,384 B below the heap ceiling. 16q’s modwork export added 32,210,944 B.
- E’s resident RSS arithmetic passed at both post-retime boundaries with 3/3 ownership identities. Candidate physical footprint rose 4.8G → 4.9G → 5.0G, while the reused reference rounded to 4.7G at all three reads. Candidate vmmap writable regions marked swapped out grew from 2.7G to 3.4G while ps RSS fell.
- F’s flattened geometry shows in the Position[]/Double[] counts. FrozenLink counted 27,930 / 41,895 / 27,930 across the reads and mutable definitions counted 13,965 / 13,965 / 13,965. The 27,930 before and timed counts are two 13,965-link sets. The whole-graph census reports the combined type counts across owners.
- Largest reported root changes present in both F reads · `runtime.simulation` +5,896,064 B, `static.BlendshapeBake.scratch` +1,034,512 B, `runtime.ordinaryOwnershipIndex` +146,720 B, `static.RetainedCensus.Layouts` +61,928 B, `static.BodyMerge.poses` +53,824 B, `static.BodyMerge.finalPoses` +32,768 B. Root changes describe first-reach attribution.
- The prescribed combined window created the retained `runtime.gcSampler` root after F’s before-read. It accounted for 873,824 B in both after-reads. Subtracting it for attribution leaves +7,296,016 B of whole-graph growth. The check uses the full census delta. Simulation got 600 s of play at 2× between reads, from day 2 at 15:30 to about 19:50.
- `RouteLeg` increased from 4,197 to 17,915 objects (+1,426,672 B) during that interval. The combined link-definition count returned from 55,860 immediately after 2→1 to its before-read count of 41,895 at road +30 s. The extra definition set at the first read was transient. The timed census was 2,715,976 B below 16q’s timed read despite growing from a smaller before-read.

That per-object size comes from the exported RouteLeg rows. The ceiling retains the uncertainty of a missing count. The travelling count from the last population summary covers residents and is periodic.
The PC manifest advanced 30.010035 game minutes between the final settled read and the repeat.
City graph growth from R1 to the final settled checkpoint, after subtracting RouteLeg bytes, was 2.223176–2.383128 MB. The interval reflects the censored R1 count.
The forced-live gap uses the same recorded 15:30 no-mod start throughout. The later checkpoint clocks advance with play. These observations apply the leak rule to the sampled series without identifying a cause for the growth.

After the drain, RouteLeg retimed minus control was -5,310. The matched summary counted 174 travelling residents at a 0.011407 minute offset. The population manifest counted 1,209 active visitors, for an upper bound of 1,383 total in-flight journeys. The rig exposes active visitors without their travelling subset. The RouteLeg result is unresolved when the excess falls between those bounds.
The retained census exports 48 top types by bytes. For a missing RouteLeg row with zero census failures, the smallest retained type’s bytes divided by the observed 104 B per RouteLeg bounds its count. The proof uses exact counts where the row is present and intervals where it is absent.

### NOT RUN

- GR-5 locked-PC and 60 fps arms. The shared Mac was the only host used. PC 19c is historical.
- #246 check 4 and the unrentable fixture. Scope was limited to #325 checks 1–7.
- #293 save checks. Rig 16h passed. #325 leaves the save path unchanged.
- #295 donor checks and inspector timing. Prior evidence is in rig 16i / 16k-donor and 16l.
- Standalone F and separate night census. L covers R0/R1. B follows the ordered conditioning and heap bracket.
- Fresh no-mod 01:00 and RSS arms. Matching historical references were available.
- Fresh no-mod 2× day arm. The 16v window plan permits recapture of cached arms with changed inputs. There is no cached 2× reference.

C followed B 20× in the same process. The city was positioned at x=215, z=0. GC sampler measuring before / after false / false. Sampler pause fields and diagnostic collection frames are unavailable with the sampler off. The PC phase recorder stayed active for C.

| 9 | 60.5789 / 120.722992 / 180.547622 / 240.602095 / 300.701921 / 360.597361 / 420.711006 / 480.73433 / 540.544088 | 200.3390479 / 400.4448886 | true / true | — |

The direct retime subphase maximum is a dash because the C phase recorder keeps only the 16 slowest frames, and for each one only its longest sub-segment. None of those retained longest sub-segments was a retime subphase, so the export has no direct retime reading. The 6.137 ms bound comes from the `top_frames` rows of the C street phase export, using the PC 19c method: bound = max(largest `sub_ms` over the 16 retained rows, `mod_ms` of the 16th retained row) + 0.001 ms for rounding, so that maximum was 6.136 ms. On a retained frame, every sub-segment, retime included, is no longer than that frame's longest sub-segment, which is its `sub_ms`. An omitted frame is no slower than the 16th retained frame, so its whole mod work, and any retime sub-segment inside it, is at most that row's `mod_ms`. The report did not copy which of the two inputs set the 6.136 ms maximum or the other input's value; both are in the C street phase export in the raw evidence directory. Route rebuild slowest update was 4.3 ms in the retime logs.

Cache root cells give bound / objects / bytes / routes / route legs.

The L verdict follows the leak rule's repeated-cycle test. From R0 to R2 the gaps do not rise steadily (RouteLeg −1,092 / −476 / −532; Mono used and forced-live fall), so the repeated growth is measured from R2. From R2 through R5, the raw RouteLeg gap (−532 / 871 / 1,251 / 1,643), the Mono used gap (4,317,184 / 5,713,920 / 8,351,744 / 9,547,776 B) and the forced-live gap (4,419,584 / 5,623,808 / 8,425,472 / 9,969,664 B) each rose at every matched retime checkpoint. The steps did not shrink steadily (RouteLeg +1,403 / +380 / +392; forced-live +1,204,224 / +2,801,664 / +1,544,192 B), so this is a fail and not NOT ESTABLISHED. The drain read is reported separately. All three gaps fell at drain (933 RouteLeg, 7,147,520 B used, 7,143,424 B forced-live) but stayed above their R2 values. Retained census bytes did not rise across R2 to R5 (−746,344 / −280,168 / −306,080 / −254,864 B). They reached a new gap maximum only at drain (217,560 B, 395,712 B above the earlier maximum). Because that is one rise after the last cycle, it is reported and does not count toward the verdict. The RouteLeg gap outside current journeys and caches was 0 at every read except −23 at R3, so the raw RouteLeg growth sits in current journeys and the named caches.

Unity ProfilerRecorder supplies GC.Collect durations and Unity frame IDs. Full profiler interval capture of paired PersistentCity.GcFrameStamp samples requires a development player. For sampler and marker records with the same Unity frame, the arithmetic range allows GC.Collect to overlap any part of UpdateCity and LateUpdate. The range is provisional because the marker intervals cannot be clipped to the sampler timestamps. The probe reports measured outside-mod subsystem excess separately. Off-CPU ≥30 ms is host or synchronization wait. The specific wait source requires a scheduler trace.

Foreground host captures use the rig sample backend. They preserve the sample call graph, ps -M, top and pmset output. All twelve captures mark thermal, performance and CPU power readbacks as unrecorded, and the captures record no reason. The night schedule was fixed before B began, using 17b’s collection times. Wait-leaf samples count stack observations. ps -M provides no stable thread IDs for before/after CPU deltas.

Wall and monotonic clocks were calibrated at both ends of the run (9.943 ms offset change). Collection overlap is shown only where the probe’s first frame validated the timebase and the sample timestamps fit the command envelope. An overlapping aggregate stack report cannot identify the stack of a particular collection frame.

B 60× planning observation: the population summary at game minute 4383.5 reported a 34.113 ms planning-slice maximum and a 34.114 ms route-planning advance unit maximum, tracked independently. It counted one gen0 collection across the slowest AdvancePopulation call; that count is at call scope and does not place the collection inside the route-planning unit. The summary was emitted inside the 600 s window, 3.5 game minutes after its 01:00 start at minute 4380. The six B 60× collection rows cover every collection in the window (probe and sampler gen0 6, collections terminal true), and none has UpdateCity above 0.617 ms. The union, PC phase and advance-call ledgers, which cover only frames inside the window, have zero counts. From these ledgers it is inferred that the slow call ran before the window opened; the evidence does not establish that it ran during the 60× approach. The summary gives no frame number, so the frame and the collection's exact placement are unresolved.

The L verdict rests on the RouteLeg[] outside caches and runtime.simulation Double[] series. The aggregate Double[] acceleration comes from the static validation buffer, which grew once from 2,080 to 4,128 B with an unchanged object count. The traffic drain differences are live traffic: the retimed arm had 9 live vehicles and routes against 7 in the control, and 719 live traffic legs against 714, with none outside live traffic and caches.

Rig 17b Mono heap gaps at R3/R4/R5 were 62.03 / 68.09 / 70.11 MB and 28.20 MB after drain. Its post-drain census gaps were TrafficRouteLeg −99/−6,336 B, TrafficVehicleState +1/+112 B, List<TrafficRouteLeg> +1/+40 B and Int32[] +15/+392 B. The 17b traffic ledger used the same census semantics as 17c.

Rig 17a finished with raw RouteLeg gaps of +185 at R5 and −1,917 at drain. At drain, TrafficRouteLeg was −39 and Int32[] was equal by count. PR #344 attributes forecast-pool vehicle copies and route lists to cache.traffic.projection. The 17a and 17b TrafficVehicleState and List<TrafficRouteLeg> drain results use different census definitions, which preclude direct comparison. The 17a report has no traffic_vehicles ledger and lacks the four new per-root views.

16z finished with raw RouteLeg gaps of +1,643 at R5 and +933 at drain. Its TrafficRouteLeg gap at drain was +4 and Int32[] was +17.

## Rig results — 23 November 2026 c, Mac (rig 17d, #350 gate-bounds checks at ce8c514d)

**0 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 1 FAIL / 1 NOT RUN** across [PR #350's three checks](https://github.com/PeterHartwieg/big-ambitions-persistent-city/pull/350). Pointer, hover and visual feel are **NOT RUN (for Peter)**, outside those counts.

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Fallback tally | **FAIL** | The requested warning appeared zero times at load, during 60 wall seconds from day 2 15:00 to 15:16 at 1x, or through shutdown. Two periodic dependency checks fell in the tally log, and the subsequent population summary recorded 1.593 ms maximum for the door check. The expected construction line was missing, so the fallback count and door names are unknown. |
| 2. Hamptons private gate | **PARTIAL** | The live map listed 12 Hamptons residential properties for sale. The building read for 1 East Hamptons Way reported private-fence index 0. The survey showed its closed driveway gate and the driveway leading to a junction with another barrier. Seven screenshots over 193 wall seconds (day 2 15:44–16:39) showed no gate crossing or moving traffic at the junction. Citywide counts varied, but the rig could not locate those vehicles on this road or confirm the segment's public classification. The open-gate arm was **NOT RUN** because the bridge exposed no gate interaction. |
| 3. Footprint gates | **NOT RUN** | The live building op exposed residential collider bounds. Neither it nor the mod inspector exposed each gate's chosen source, its expanded box, or public-road segment positions. The footprint-gate inventory, intersections and local stops or detours remain unknown. |

In `PublicRoadAccess`, the constructor compares the new fallback-name array with an empty array when no previous snapshot exists. An empty tally therefore produces no initial warning. This explains how the missing line can occur. The live rig could not independently confirm a zero fallback-gate count or exercise the unchanged, nonempty warning path.

The bridge's `use {"op":"list","radius":12}` returned `"things":[]` at the gate approach `(-2808, 0.06, -1463)`. The 40 m query from the driveway also returned no targets. The installed rig operation catalog supplied no gate toggle. `pc road status`, `pc gate status` and `pc traffic status` each returned `Warning: [Persistent City] Unknown command. Use: pc population census [workplaces] | pc population person <id> | pc population manifest`. The bridge rejected the read `crew_drive_probe {"op":"waypoints","ids":[0]}` with `Unknown command 'crew_drive_probe'.` These are readout and interaction limits.

Foreground host captures use the rig sample backend. They preserve the sample call graph, ps -M, top and pmset output. The night schedule was fixed before B began, using 17b’s collection times. Wait-leaf samples count stack observations. ps -M provides no stable thread IDs for before/after CPU deltas.

Wall and monotonic clocks were calibrated at both ends of the run (1.923 ms offset change). Collection overlap is shown only where the probe’s first frame validated the timebase and the sample timestamps fit the command envelope. An overlapping aggregate stack report cannot identify the stack of a particular collection frame.

### L — repeated retime versus 1× control

Each complete 1→2→1 pair waited for the commit and the new road snapshot. The settle interval starts at the return-to-1× road snapshot. The helper matches the control at native minutes and takes another read after the 30-game-minute drain. The final retime and drain are compared with their preceding maxima. The helper flags a series when its final three cycle steps all rise to a new maximum; a shorter rise leaves the plateau unestablished. Under the GR-5 leak rule a flagged series fails unless slowing leaves the available cycles unable to tell continued growth from a plateau, in which case the verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED (rig 17c applied this). The three flagged series do not meet that exception. Mono used steps were +69,632 / +2,244,608 / +1,015,808 B and forced-live +831,488 / +1,638,400 / +1,273,856 B, so each final step was larger than the first. RouteLeg[] outside caches steps were +1,496 / +512 / +1,136 B: the increase accelerated on the final cycle and grew further at drain, to 7,272 B. The cycles show continued growth, so L stays FAIL.

The rig ran game build 3682 and RLO 1.0.6 at 1× in `FT RIGTMP-GATE-24b-mac`, a byte-identical copy of `FT GR5 13f Timing v1` with 1,000 residents and 2,000 visitors. The scene had four closed, locked Hamptons vehicle gates. The run held `gate:-2902.5:0.0:-1515.5`, private-fence index 0. Persistent City reported `source=collider`, `public_road=no` and a 29,010-node road snapshot. The gate settled and stayed locked in both holds. Gate-op errors were zero.

**First live use of `vehicle_route`.** The position-based target snapped to the parallel lane. The planner returned a 356.33 m loop, and both cars entered the 6 m arrival radius from the start lane before completing the loop. The repeat used explicit same-lane waypoints 16447 → 15163 and returned a 41.79 m path. All four public-road drives had zero read failures and track breaks. The closest observed approach to the selected gate was 50.02 m. Both through plans used the same start near (-2960, 0, -1519) and target probe near (-2902.5, 0, -1510). The Gley planner returned no crossing leg in either state before any through car could spawn.

**Cleanup.** Across 24 pre-spawn and 28 post-release local overlap reads, traffic collider counts were zero. Immediately before each release, the overlap centred on the injected car saw its `BodyCollider` and `FrontTrigger` (2 → 0). Other positive reads overlapped that same car. Each `release` used `RemoveVehicle` on the tracked car in slot 19, and route status changed from live to `removed` with zero removal errors. `release all` found zero live routes. No ambient car removal was observed. The collider op supplies counts and collider names and has no ambient vehicle ID field. The repeated use of slot 19 was across injected cars. Ambient reuse within 50 m was unobserved. Final scene-wide held gates were zero.

`FT-E6-Vendors` and `FT-E6-Vendors-base` held cart A with a Hot Dog Grill and truck B with an Industrial Grill. Persistent City reported 1,000 citizens. The FT commissary delivered and restocked hot dogs, burgers and kabobs. The weekday route settings separated the snapped stops by 416.8 m for A and 384.8 m for B. Brewed Beans at 20 3rd Street supplied the rival fingerprint. The cart and player shop were about 36 m apart.
